references.text: Israel's elders ask Samuel to appoint a king over them, just as all other nations have. This shows that the choice of king should be in accordance with God's will.
The Lord tells Samuel that He will send him a man from Benjamin who is to be anointed as prince over Israel. This illustrates that God chooses the king.
Samuel presents Saul as the one the Lord has chosen to be king. This fulfills the requirement that the king must be chosen by the Lord.
The Lord sends Samuel to anoint one of Jesse's sons as king. God Himself chooses who will be king over Israel.
All the tribes of Israel come to David in Hebron and anoint him king over Israel. David was from the tribe of Judah, a brother among brothers.
Jeroboam, a non-Davidic king, is installed as king over the northern kingdom. The text shows the consequences of political division in Israel.
Hosea condemns Israel for appointing kings without the Lord's approval. This emphasizes the importance of God choosing the king.
God promises Abraham that kings will come from him. Israel's kings were to be of Abraham's lineage, thus brothers.
Balaam's prophecy about a star from Jacob and a scepter from Israel. A future king from within Israel.
Jesus declares that His kingdom is not of this world and confirms that He is king. He is the ultimate fulfillment of the God-chosen king.
